AMUSEMENTS IN MATHEMATICS.

    "Some quoted line."

    OLIVER WENDELL HOLMES.


MONEY PUZZLES.


1.--A POST-OFFICE PERPLEXITY.

A lady asked for change of a crown in pence and shillings, and the
clerk was perplexed. How many ways could it be done?


2.--YOUTHFUL PRECOCITY.

A boy of 12 had saved 3s. 4d. by the age of ten years old. What did
he save each year?
3. This line starts with a number but is prose, not a puzzle.


GREEK CROSS PUZZLES.


3.--THE CROSS AND THE SQUARE.

Cut a Greek cross into four pieces that will fit together and form a
perfect square. The cut lines may be drawn on the figure.

[Illustration]

A NOTE IN CAPITALS INSIDE THE TEXT
continues on the next line and must stay part of puzzle 3.


4.--THE SQUARE OF CROSSES.

Here is a figure of five crosses arranged in a grid.

SOLUTIONS.


MONEY PUZZLES.


1.--It can be done in 1,000 different ways when the coins are taken as
listed.

2.--YOUTHFUL PRECOCITY.

He saved 1s. 8d. each year.
3. A prose line that starts with a number must stay inside solution 2.

3.--Make two straight cuts through the centre at right angles, each
joining a corner to the middle of an opposite arm.

4.--Arrange them as in the figure.
